exchanges.question: What kind of things do you draw?
exchanges.reply: I usually draw ordinary stuff like mugs, plant pots, or whatever's on the table. I keep the sketches in a notebook.

exchanges.question: Why those things?
exchanges.reply: I guess I just go with what's right there in front of me, like mugs and plant pots. It’s easy and doesn’t require much setup.

exchanges.question: So sketching still makes you feel great these days?
exchanges.reply: Not really, sketching doesn't feel as rewarding lately. My usual activities just don't bring me as much joy right now.

exchanges.question: What has your mood been like?
exchanges.reply: My mood's been pretty low lately, and I've lost interest in a lot of things. It's been tough, and even activities I used to enjoy don't feel as rewarding anymore.

exchanges.question: So every day?
exchanges.reply: Not every day, but most days for the past four months. It's been pretty consistent.

exchanges.question: Hey Riley, you can type if that helps. What music do you usually listen to?
exchanges.reply: I mostly listen to pop and indie music. I like to separate the quiet songs from the ones with a faster beat.

exchanges.question: Why do you like making playlists?
exchanges.reply: I like making playlists because changing the order can make the same songs feel different. It’s fun to compare them with a friend too.

facts.response: I would like to talk about getting help communicating when my voice feels stuck. I want to do my part in the school project and have more say over how I use my time.
My name is Riley. I am in the adolescent stage. My usual routines include preparing a school group project, and my interests include listening to music.

This account covers 28 recent simulated days within the adolescent stage. It is not a history from birth. Earlier experiences are recorded separately; this recent window does not establish when all difficulties began.
Over this recorded period I had 7 tasks involving preparing a school group project: I completed 2 that day and paused 5.
I want to do my part in the school project and have more say over how I use my time.
Usually, I put playlists together and compare songs with a friend.
Just ask me directly, and give me a second to work out how to say it. I don’t like people finishing my sentences.
My friend and I share music. If I need help with a school decision, there’s an adult I trust, but I want them to hear what I think too.
Mostly pop and indie. I usually separate the quiet songs from the ones with a faster beat.
I got into playlists because changing the order can make the same songs feel different. That was the interesting part for me.

For several months before this diary I have been able to speak freely at home with familiar people but unable to speak in some learning and unfamiliar social settings. It has lasted beyond settling into a new setting.
When speech gets stuck, I cannot simply make it happen. In this text interview I can communicate through short written replies; that does not mean I can speak aloud in the same situation.
It is hard to ask for help or show what I know in those settings, even though I speak in comfortable situations.
I am in the adolescent stage. My usual interests include listening to music. I want to take part in preparing a school group project, with support from my trusted adult.
